name: Palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7

lead: Palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 (sold as Rigin) is a lab-made peptide with a fatty acid tail, used in anti-aging and sensitive-skin products. People use it for smoother, calmer-looking skin. It is paired with palmitoyl tripeptide-1 in Matrixyl 3000.

It is described as an anti-inflammatory signal peptide: in lab models it is reported to reduce IL-6 release, which would mean less inflammation-driven collagen breakdown. Its effects in people have mostly been studied inside multi-ingredient products rather than on its own. Peptides in general are widely used in sensitive-skin products, per an analysis of 88 facial cosmetics.

paras: It is used in daily serums and creams, typically in blends with other peptides, and applied to the face and neck. Results from such products are usually judged over weeks to months.
Sold as a cosmetic ingredient; labels advise external use only and avoiding the eyes. No ingredient-specific safety data were found.

angle.text: Palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 (Rigin) is an anti-inflammatory signal peptide in anti-aging and sensitive-skin products, aimed at smoother, calmer skin. It is reported in lab models to dampen IL-6, limiting inflammation-driven collagen breakdown. Little isolated human data exist.

lead: Palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 (Pal-GQPR, sold as Rigin) is a synthetic peptide of glycine, glutamine, proline and arginine attached to palmitic acid and used in anti-aging and sensitive-skin cosmetics. [1] It is described as an anti-inflammatory signal peptide and is the second peptide in Matrixyl 3000. [1]

Grokipedia, an AI-generated source, reports it decreases IL-6 secretion in lab models. [1] Peptides in general are widely used in sensitive-skin products, according to an analysis of 88 facial cosmetics. [2] Published human efficacy data specific to this peptide are limited.

paras: The palmitoyl group raises lipophilicity to aid passage through the stratum corneum. [1] It appears in multi-peptide formulations; US labels list it with other peptides in stretch mark creams. [3]

Reported laboratory effects include lowering IL-6 after stressors such as UVB, and promoting basement membrane proteins. [1] A study of dermal extracellular matrix and the epidermal-dermal junction examined effects of age and peptide applications using imaging methods. [4]
A 2026 study applied serums with both Matrixyl 3000 peptides to three volunteers and detected both in stratum corneum layers with signal decreasing with depth. [5]

A study of a multi-component eye cream containing palmitoyl tripeptide-1 and palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 alongside other actives evaluated efficacy and safety in the periorbital area, so effects cannot be assigned to one ingredient. [6] No trial of this peptide alone was found.
